38.25.0.en: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder [25].

38.25.1.en: It seems to man as though there were no restraint upon the rains, nor on the gathering of waters in branching channels, nor when the waters flood many lands as though they had departed from obedience to God who determined their course.

38.25.2.en: All things proceed by divine permission, and it is said of the king's heart that it is in the hand of God as the rivers of water, he turneth it whithersoever he will (Prov 21:1).

38.25.3.en: And as God directs the streams of water, so He has authority over the course of the lightnings.

38.26.0.en: To cause it to rain on the earth, where no man is; on the wilderness, wherein there is no man [26].

38.26.1.en: If God determines even the places of the rain, then in His care for His creation He allows rain even in places not inhabited by people, so that the wild beasts may find water, or if a traveler passes through.

38.27.0.en: To satisfy the desolate and waste ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth? [27]

38.27.1.en: Although God cares for man in a special way, He does not ignore the lowly creatures in the wildernesses, and the beasts of prey. As the psalmist says: "He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills. They give drink to every beast of the field: the wild asses (the wild donkey) quench their thirst" (Ps 104:10-11).

38.28.0.en: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew? [28]

38.28.1.en: He had previously spoken of the great sea as a child that came forth from the womb at God's command, swaddled by Him with mist and clothed with clouds, as though God were like a nurse even to the lifeless sea. Now he speaks of the dew, the uncounted drops, and portrays them as a newborn for whom God cares, even for a drop of dew! He is at work in all nature by His surpassing good nature.

38.28.2.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that God often uses the expression of birth even for lifeless creatures, to affirm that no creature came about by chance, but all things are in the mind of God, who is wholly love and care.

38.28.3.en: * [Who is the father of the rain?! And who hath begotten the drops of dew?!] (Job 38:28)

38.28.4.en: Who condensed the air into clouds, and bound them to carry the waters of the rains, so that they come golden in color (Job 37:22) from the south, in one order at one time, and in many circles and diverse shapes at another?!

38.28.5.en: "Who can number the clouds in wisdom?" (Job 38:37), for it is said in Job that He knows the parting of the clouds?! (Job 33:16) LXX.

38.28.6.en: Who is "he that bringeth forth the wind out of his treasuries" (Ps 135:7), and as we said before [Who begot the drops of dew, and out of whose womb came the snow?!] (Ps 135:7; Job 38:28), for its substance is water and its strength is like stone!

38.28.7.en: At one time the water becomes snow like wool (cf. Ps 16:147), at another He scatters it as hoarfrost like ashes, and at yet another it becomes a stony substance. He rules the water as He wills.

38.28.8.en: * The nature of water is one, but its work is manifold in power, for it works in the vine as wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and in the olive tree as oil to make his face to shine, and in bread strengthens man's heart (Ps 15:104), and it is found in all kinds of fruit that God created.

38.28.9.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem Out of whose womb came the ice?

38.29.0.en: The hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it? [29]

38.29.1.en: Waters freeze into ice and snow in an extremely short time and in quantities hard or impossible to count, revealing man's inability to comprehend natural phenomena that take place before him and with a speed he does not expect. What created power is able to accomplish these wonderful phenomena?

38.29.2.en: The waters are hid as with a stone.

38.30.0.en: And the face of the deep is frozen [30].

38.30.1.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) grieves that the Jews, who used to be like the rains that water the earth, through their unbelief lost all spiritual warmth and became like cold, icy stones.

38.31.s.en: 7. His ignorance of the stars and their effect on the earth

38.31.0.en: 31 "Canst thou bind the bands of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion? 32 Canst thou bring forth the mansions in their seasons, and guide the Bier with its daughters? 33 Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?

38.31.1.en: Canst thou bind the bands of the Pleiades, or loose the cords of Orion? [31]

38.31.2.en: Since many philosophers linked the fates of men to the movements of the stars, he therefore spoke of the groups of stars, for God has created all these with wisdom, and however much man studies astronomy and comes to know some of the secrets of the stars, he has no authority over them, nor do the stars have any authority over the fates of men.

38.31.3.en: * Do you know who it is that numbers the stars and calls them by their names? Do you know the differences of glory that each of them has (1 Cor 41:15), and the order of their movement, that then I may trust you when you weave the fabric of human affairs and arm the creature against the Creator?

38.32.0.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Canst thou bring forth the mansions in their seasons, and guide the Bier with its daughters? [32]

38.32.1.en: By the mansions he means the stars that are in the south, and by the Bier the stars that are in the north. Who among men has authority to move the stars? But God alone uses them, as it is written in the book of Judges: "They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera" (Judg 5:20).

38.32.2.en: The expressions "the mansions" and "the Bier" appear in the Septuagint as Mazuroth and the evening stars; and in the text of Pope Gregory (the Great), the morning star and the evening star. The Pope sees that the morning star is the Lord Christ, who announced to us the eternal morning, who rose in the morning from the dead and shone upon us with the splendor of His light, shattering the darkness of our corruption, so that John was right to call Him "the bright and morning star" (Rev 22:16). As for the coming evening star, it is the Antichrist, whom the Lord permits to rule over the sons of the earth, over the unbelieving hearts which accept the rule of the Antichrist over them.

38.32.3.en: * The Father brought the morning star in due time, for it is written: "But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem them that were under the law" (Gal 4:4-5). Being born of a virgin, He appeared as the morning star in the midst of the darkness of our night. For having driven away the gloom of sin, He announced to us the eternal morning. But He showed Himself as the morning star because He rose in the morning from the dead, and overcame by the splendor of His light the hideousness of the darkness of our death. Fittingly John called Him "the bright and morning star" (Rev 22:16), since He appeared alive after death. He became for us the morning star. He gave us life in His person, an example of the resurrection. As He also pointed to the coming (deceptive) light. He permits the evening star to dominate the sons of the earth in that He permits the Antichrist to dominate the unbelieving hearts of the Jews... The Lord says in the Gospel: "I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive" (Jn 5:43). Paul also says: "Because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness" (2 Thess 2:10-12). Therefore the evening star will not dominate those who wished to be sons of heaven.

38.33.0.en: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth? [33]

38.33.1.en: There is no one who knows the ordinances of heaven or comprehends its mysteries and decrees. But heaven comprehends what is on earth, and the heavenly beings discover much of the mysteries of God's love and His plan toward mankind. It is as if God says to Job: "If I have permitted trials for you, you do not know what goes on in heaven, but the heavenly beings know why I permitted you afflictions, and they know my love for you and my defense of you against Satan."

38.34.s.en: 8. His ignorance of God's power in the sky and in natural phenomena

38.34.0.en: 34 Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee? 35 Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are? 36 Who hath put wisdom in the dense cloud, or who hath shown understanding in the meteors? 37 Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can pour out the bottles of heaven, 38 When the dust is cast into a mass, and the clay (the clods) cleave fast together?

38.34.1.en: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee? [34]

38.34.2.en: We have already seen that the clouds refer to the prophets of the Old Testament and the apostles of the New Testament, for God speaks through His holy men as from the clouds, and He alone covers man with the waters of His grace and the gift of His Holy Spirit.

38.34.3.en: The Lord came speaking among the clouds, where the prophets bore witness to Him and the apostles preach Him, and the peoples have received faith in Him like many waters, as though the abundance of waters had covered Him. It was not possible for righteous Job, nor for any other man of the Old Testament, to comprehend this mystery clearly as it was realized by the coming of the Lord Christ.

38.35.0.en: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we are? [35]

38.35.1.en: The clouds refer to the apostles who went about preaching the Gospel, and the lightnings that issue from the clouds are the signs and wonders that God gave to the apostles to bear witness to the divine truth. One of these lightnings issuing from the clouds is what the Apostle Peter said to the lame man: "Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk" (Acts 3:6-7).

38.35.2.en: As the clouds are subject to God, so the lightning bears witness to Him in obedience.

38.36.0.en: Who hath put wisdom in the dense cloud, or who hath shown understanding in the meteors? [36]

38.36.1.en: Some translate the dense cloud as a hurricane. As for the meteors, they are a blazing flame of fire.

38.36.2.en: The Septuagint reads: "Who gives women skill in spinning (weaving) and knowledge of embroidery?"

38.36.3.en: * Note this: He speaks of the practical side. He mixes small things with great.

38.36.4.en: St. John Chrysostom St. Ambrose sees in this phrase a reference to the weaving of the heavenly breastplate of the Lord Christ as the Great High Priest, which is woven of the power of God and His wisdom and His righteousness, and adorned with precious stones. Or it is the heavenly wedding garment adorned with various stones and woven with gold; it is the fabric of working faith.

38.37.0.en: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can pour out the bottles of heaven [37]?

38.37.1.en: "Bottles" translates the plural of the word "ziqq" (skin), that is, a flask. Can any man, however great his wisdom, number the clouds that are in the sky, and place them precisely, and determine their size and weight? And who can speak of the rains that pour from heaven as from huge flasks?

38.38.0.en: When the dust is cast into a mass, and the clay (the clods) cleave fast together? [38]

38.38.1.en: Although the wicked are like the chaff which the wind driveth away (Ps 1:4), or like the dust or dirt flying in the air, because they have no love uniting them together in the Spirit, yet God in His love gives them the spirit of love that they may cleave together like useful lumps of clay.

38.39.s.en: 9. God's care for the irrational animals

38.39.0.en: 39 "Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lioness? or fill the appetite of the young lions, 40 When they couch in their dens, and abide in the covert to lie in wait? 41 Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat?

38.39.1.en: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lioness? or fill the appetite of the young lions [39]?

38.39.2.en: The choice of these animals and birds (Job 38:39 - 41:34) was not a choice without purpose, but it may be said that they represent the procession of animals and birds hostile to human society in man's view at that time. Therefore demons were often portrayed in the forms of these animals and birds. God's care is surpassing even for the beasts of prey and the birds that attack human society. For all of these, God not only knows their ways, but they are subject to Him and He sustains them. If God cared for the lifeless creation that He brought out of nothing, and cared for the laws of the sky, the falling of snow or the blowing of winds or the falling of rains, and cares for the wild animals and the birds of prey, how then should He not care for the affairs of man, for whose sake He created all these?

38.39.3.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the lioness here refers to the proud Judaism, when it accepts faith in the Lord Christ through the preaching of the Church, for the Lord Christ Himself satisfies the souls of its children.

38.40.0.en: When they couch in their dens (when they crouch in their lairs), and abide in the covert to lie in wait? (and lurk in their thicket to lie in wait?) [40]

38.40.1.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that he speaks here of the period between the passion of the Lord Christ and the descent of the Holy Spirit on the feast of Pentecost, when the apostles and disciples ceased from ministry, so they were like the lioness that crouches in her lair and lurks in the thicket in a state of lying in wait. They were waiting, in fear of those who opposed them, until they should be clothed with power from on high to begin the preaching.

38.40.2.en: They resemble the lioness who stays in her lair with the little cubs until the lion brings the prey to them.

38.41.0.en: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat? [41]

38.41.1.en: Wonderful is God in His care and providence for His creation, for He cares even for the young ravens, and gives them their food (Ps 147:9). Man cares for the creatures useful to him, but God cares for all creation. He listens even to the cry (croaking) of the young ravens.

38.41.2.en: It is said that ravens do not care for their young, so the young croak as though to God, and God gives them their food. They teach us to cry "Abba, Father" (Rom 8:15), for He hears us even if our parents do not hear us. As the psalmist says: [When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up] (a).

38.41.3.en: If He likened the Jews who were coming to faith to the lioness whose cubs' needs God satisfies, then He likens the Gentiles to the ravens, and God cares for these and those: "He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry" (Ps 147:9).

38.41.4.en: * The animals receive their food when beastlike minds feed upon Holy Scripture. But food is given to the young ravens, that is, to the sons of the Gentiles, when their longings are refreshed by our conversations with them... The young ravens, that is, the holy preachers coming from the Church of the Gentiles, truly do not rely on themselves but on the power of their Savior; therefore it was well said: [when his young ones cry unto God], for they realize that they can do nothing by their own strength.

38.41.6.en: Grant me to perceive the greatness of Your providence

38.41.7.en: * For my sake You laid the foundations of the earth, and set it up as upon pillars.

38.41.8.en: None knows its hidden mysteries but You.

38.41.9.en: The heavenly beings looked upon Your works for my sake, and came forward like a harmonious chorus, sang and praised with a spirit of exultation, and all shouted because of Your love and care!

38.41.10.en: You set boundaries for the sea.

38.41.11.en: You shut it in as with barricades and doors.

38.41.12.en: You broke its haughtiness and the pride of its deeps!

38.41.13.en: Let me go down to the depths of the sea and walk about, and be amazed by its hidden treasures.

38.41.14.en: * With every dawn I stand in amazement, I see the sparks of light begin to shine.

38.41.15.en: Who can determine its place? Who can measure its dimensions?

38.41.16.en: What a mighty and wonderful Creator You are!

38.41.17.en: * The sun rises to give joy to the earth; with every morning I see it as though it were new!

38.41.18.en: I touch in the rays of the sun the splendor of Your grace.

38.41.19.en: My soul exults in Your daily works!

38.41.20.en: * I look at the clouds; who can comprehend their size!

38.41.22.en: Even the storms and the snow and the ice, all of them do not escape Your hand.

38.41.24.en: * All nature You make subject to me, You care even for the rains to water the earth for me.

38.41.25.en: How wonderful! You do not ignore even the wild beasts of the wilderness!

38.41.26.en: You care for me as a king whom You set up on the earth, and You care for the animals and the birds; even lifeless creation is an object of Your care!

38.41.27.en: You provide the beasts of prey with food in the wilderness or in the forest.

38.41.28.en: And You hear the croaking of the young ravens, and You sustain them!

38.41.29.en: Glory to You, O Shepherd of all, in Your love!
